title: Adaptive region affinity using decay-weighted latency histograms and prioritized fallback variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive region selection mechanism that uses recent latency telemetry (decay-weighted histograms for p50/p95) plus network health scoring to set per-customer region affinity and dynamic tier routing. The system should also prioritize fallback model variants (e.g., quantized or lower-context variants) when region health or latency SLOs degrade.

Summary of approach:
- Collect per-region latency samples (per-customer, per-model, per-route) and maintain decay-weighted histograms with configurable decay half-life (default 5 minutes). From the histogram compute p50 and p95 windows.
- Compute a composite network_health_score that mixes p95 latency tail, recent error rate (5m), packet loss / proxy-level failures, and capacity pressure (region utilization). Weighting is configurable but default: 50% p95 tail percentile score, 30% error-rate, 20% capacity pressure.
- Region affinity decision: rank candidate regions by a combined score = alpha * latency_score + beta * health_score + gamma * cost_score + delta * region_rtt_penalty. Default alpha=0.5, beta=0.3, gamma=0.15, delta=0.05. Provide ability to pin region or set multi-preference list for fast failover.
- Tier routing: within a region prefer higher-tier GPUs for latency-sensitive traffic; use smart throttling to spill to lower tiers when cost pressure is detected, but only if the health score and p95 thresholds remain within limits.
- Fallback model variants: define per-model fallback chains (e.g., float16 -> int8 -> int4 quantized) with quality regression budgets per-tenant. When a region's composite score crosses a configured threshold, the runtime will first attempt region fallback (route to alternative region), then fallback model variant within the same region, then escalate to cross-region serving based on policy.

Operational constraints and observability:
- Expose metrics: region.p50, region.p95, region.ewma_latency, region.health_score, region.error_rate, region.utilization, fallback.invocations, fallback.quality_delta, route.decisions_count.
- Add tracing tags for route.decider=(metric-driven|pinned|manual), selected_region, fallback_variant, reason_code.
- Add dashboards for per-tenant and aggregated views; add regression alerts when fallback rate increases > 1% over baseline for 5m.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement telemetry ingestion and histogram logic behind a feature flag (opt-in).
2) Deploy scoring and simulation mode: decisions are logged but not acted upon. Collect 2 weeks of simulated decisions.
3) Run canary (5% traffic) with active routing for low-risk tenants. Monitor latency, error rates, fallback rates.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% then global as metrics validate.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- System computes p50/p95 and a normalized health score for each region within 60s of telemetry arrival.
- Routing decisions are made within the existing routing latency SLO (<10ms added decision time).
- Fallback policy executes and records metrics; fallback quality regressions remain below per-tenant budgets during canary.
- Dashboards and alerts present clear signals; ops runbook created for fallback surge and region outage.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Using decay-weighted histograms favors recent performance but can be noisy; we mitigate with minimum sample counts and smoothing.
- Prioritizing p95 reduces tail latency but may increase cost due to cross-region routing; provide configuration knobs per-tenant.
- Falling back to lower-precision variants reduces cost and latency but may hurt output quality; enforce per-tenant quality budgets and allow explicit allowlists for fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Latency histograms (decay-weighted) compute p50/p95 within 60s for active regions
Composite health_score generated every 30s per region and stored in time-series DB
Routing decision added <10ms to request path when enabled (measured in canary)
Fallback chain triggers and metrics are emitted; fallback rate and quality_delta visible in dashboard
Simulation mode shows expected route changes without impacting live traffic
Ops runbook and escalation path written and reviewed by SRE and Support
